title: The Rink to the Ledger: A Child Actor, the Gold Farms, and a Candidate Who Did Not Need to Win
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Child on the Ice: Minnesota and the Studio Years

stops.name: Minneapolis, born on the fourteenth of November
stops.date_confidence: attested; birth date and city given consistently in the reachable biographical record
stops.campa: Brock Jeffrey Pierce is born in Minneapolis on the fourteenth of November, 1980. Before he can read he is working: television commercials, a toddler set in front of a camera and paid for the hour. No source gives the date of that first employment, only that it began early and that it was steady. Minnesota in these years is a hockey state with a film office. The commercials keep coming through his childhood, and the first credit anyone can date is a hockey picture released when he is eleven.
suggested_refs: Minneapolis in the early 1980s, a regional market for national television commercials

stops.name: Minneapolis, young Gordon Bombay
stops.date_confidence: release year attested, month set to 01 by convention; the Little Big League credit appears on Pierce's own article and not in that film's cast list, and nothing in the reachable record places him personally at the Metrodome
stops.campa: He is eleven when The Mighty Ducks is released and he is in it, playing Gordon Bombay as a boy: the flashback child whose missed penalty shot is the wound the rest of the picture exists to heal. Two years later he returns to the part in D2, whose championship finale is shot at the brand new Arrowhead Pond in Anaheim before fifteen thousand people and a shifting wall of cardboard cutouts. That arena floor belongs to the adult cast. Pierce is in the flashback. Between 1992 and 1997 he works steadily, six features in five years.
suggested_refs: The Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome, Minneapolis, staging ground for the Little Big League finale

stops.name: Richmond, the president's son
stops.date_confidence: release year attested, month set to 01 by convention; Richmond location shooting attested for the production, though no source itemizes Pierce's own shooting days
stops.campa: First Kid casts him as Luke Davenport, the son of a sitting president, and films most of its Washington in Richmond, Virginia: the same Federal columns, cheaper permits, no actual White House. Pierce is fifteen and carrying a studio picture, playing a boy who lives in the residence and resents the agent assigned to guard him. Richmond doubles for the capital scene by scene. Twenty-four years later he will file with the Federal Election Commission to run for the office his character's father held.
suggested_refs: Richmond, Virginia, standing in for Washington in First Kid (1996)

stops.name: Los Angeles, the last credits
stops.date_confidence: The Ride is attested as a 1997 credit and the last one; month set to 01 by convention
stops.campa: The Ride is released in 1997 and it is the last credit. Ripper Man, Problem Child 3: Junior in Love, Three Wishes and Earth Minus Zero are already behind him, five years of steady work, and at sixteen he stops. Child actors mostly stop because the work stops, and the reachable record does not say which way it went here; it says only that it ended. What the record does say is where he goes next. Within a year he is in Santa Monica, on a salary of a quarter of a million dollars and holding one percent of a company building television for the internet.
suggested_refs: The 1995-1997 credits: Ripper Man, Problem Child 3, Three Wishes, Earth Minus Zero, The Ride

segments.name: Santa Monica: The Network That Was Going to Be Television

stops.name: Encino, the house of Marc Collins-Rector
stops.date_confidence: the source says Pierce joined Collins-Rector and Shackley at age sixteen, which falls between November 1996 and November 1997; the month here orders the segment and is not attested. The street address of the mansion is not confirmed in the reachable record; the pin is Encino generally
stops.campa: At sixteen he leaves acting to join Marc Collins-Rector and Chad Shackley, who are building a company to put programming on the internet before the internet can carry it. He lives with them at a Los Angeles mansion in the San Fernando Valley where the parties are held. Collins-Rector is thirty-six. The house will be named repeatedly in litigation over the fifteen years that follow, and the exact street is not confirmed in anything reachable, only the fact of the arrangement and who was living inside it.
suggested_refs: The Los Angeles mansion of Marc Collins-Rector, cited in the DEN-related civil suits

stops.name: Santa Monica, the network established
stops.date_confidence: the company is dated to 1998 in the reachable record while Pierce's own biography puts his joining at age sixteen, which is 1996 or 1997; the two statements are not reconciled by any source and both are left standing. Month set to 01 by convention
stops.campa: Digital Entertainment Network incorporates in Santa Monica in 1998: three men and a plan to make short episodic video for young audiences, over dial-up connections that cannot yet carry it. Pierce is eighteen and one of the founders. He holds one percent of the shares and draws two hundred and fifty thousand dollars a year, which is more than any of the films paid him. Los Angeles in 1998 is full of such companies. For about eighteen months this is the one everybody believes in.
suggested_refs: The Digital Entertainment Network offices in Santa Monica, 1998-2000

stops.name: Santa Monica, twenty-six million dollars
stops.date_confidence: attested to May 1999; day set to 01 by convention
stops.campa: In May of 1999 the company raises twenty-six million dollars from Microsoft, Dell and Chase Capital Partners. In September Microsoft names it a partner in the Windows Media Broadband Jumpstart initiative. A public offering is scheduled for October at seventy-five million dollars. Pierce is not yet nineteen. The offices fill with people who have left television for it. In the edit bays the episodes are finished and stacked, waiting on household connections that cannot carry them.
suggested_refs: The Windows Media Broadband Jumpstart initiative, September 1999

stops.name: Santa Monica, the offering withdrawn
stops.date_confidence: lawsuit filed October 1999, resignations November 1999, both attested to the month; days set to 01 by convention
stops.campa: In October a lawsuit is filed alleging that Collins-Rector sexually molested a minor over three years beginning in 1993. The public offering is withdrawn. In November all three of them resign: Collins-Rector, Shackley, Pierce. Pierce is nineteen and has been out of the film business for two years. The money raised in May is still in the company and the company no longer has a future. What it has instead is a set of allegations that will attach to every name on the masthead for the next quarter century.
suggested_refs: The withdrawn DEN initial public offering, scheduled October 1999 at 75 million dollars

stops.name: Santa Monica, the doors close
stops.date_confidence: layoffs attested to February 2000, bankruptcy filing to June 2000; day set to 01 by convention
stops.campa: The staff are let go in February. In June the company files for bankruptcy and shuts down. Two years earlier it had Microsoft's money, a standing item in the trade press and a studio lot's worth of programming nobody could stream; it now has a receiver and a list of creditors. Marc Collins-Rector leaves the country. Chad Shackley leaves with him. Brock Pierce, nineteen years old and holding one percent of nothing, leaves with them both, and the three of them are next attested together on the southern coast of Spain.
suggested_refs: The DEN bankruptcy filing, June 2000

stops.name: Los Angeles, the suit of the three employees
stops.date_confidence: attested to July 2000; day set to 01 by convention. Sources report the claims against Pierce as dismissed and as settled out of court without agreeing which, and both readings are left standing here
stops.campa: In July three former employees sue Collins-Rector and Pierce, alleging that drugs were supplied and sex pressured at company gatherings. The claims against Pierce are dismissed, or settled out of court; the reachable sources give both and do not agree. In 2011 the plaintiffs are reported to have been awarded judgment and interest above three million dollars against the parties still in the case. Pierce is out of the country for most of the litigation, and has been since the bankruptcy.
suggested_refs: The 2000 civil actions against Collins-Rector and Pierce, and the reported 2011 judgment

stops.name: Marbella, the villa on the coast
stops.date_confidence: the relocation to Spain is attested as a range, roughly 2000 to 2002; the month here orders the segment and is not attested
stops.campa: After the collapse the three of them relocate to Spain, to a villa on the Costa del Sol. Marbella in these years is a coastline of foreign nationals and few questions, an hour from Gibraltar and a long way from a Los Angeles courthouse. Pierce is twenty, out of the United States, and the California litigation proceeds without him. He does not go back to acting and he does not go back to Los Angeles. The business he starts from this address will be headquartered in Hong Kong within the year.
suggested_refs: The Marbella villa shared by Collins-Rector, Shackley and Pierce, 2000-2002

stops.name: Central, Hong Kong, Internet Gaming Entertainment
stops.date_confidence: founding year attested, month set to 01 by convention; the Hong Kong headquarters and customer service centre are attested for the company's peak years rather than specifically for 2001
stops.campa: Internet Gaming Entertainment is founded in 2001, with headquarters and a customer service centre in Hong Kong. The product is virtual money: gold and currency earned inside massively multiplayer games, bought from the people who grind it out and sold to the people who will not. It is legal, and it violates the terms of service of every publisher whose game it touches. It works immediately. The company's early paperwork lists an address in Marbella, which is where its twenty-year-old founder happens to be living.
suggested_refs: The IGE headquarters and customer service centre in Hong Kong

stops.name: Marbella, the raid of the seventeenth of May
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: On the seventeenth of May, 2002, Interpol raids the villa and arrests Marc Collins-Rector. Pierce, twenty-one, has been sharing the house. He is not among those arrested. What the raid ends is the arrangement that began when he was sixteen in a mansion in the San Fernando Valley: six years of living in the same houses as the man he went into business with at the end of his childhood. He leaves Spain. Nothing in the reachable record charges him in connection with the raid, and nothing in it says where he lives for the four years that follow.
suggested_refs: The Interpol raid on the Marbella villa, 17 May 2002

stops.name: Shanghai, where the gold is farmed
stops.date_confidence: the Shanghai office is attested for the company's peak years without a founding date; 2004 is chosen to sit alongside the attested 2004-2005 acquisition spree, and the month is set to 01 by convention
stops.campa: IGE keeps an office in Shanghai. The supply side of the trade sits here: rooms of players paid by the hour, running characters through the same repeatable tasks to produce currency that is sold on to Western customers at a markup. The press calls it gold farming. Between 2004 and 2005 the company spends more than twenty-five million dollars buying out seven smaller competitors, and by 2005 it is estimated to hold roughly half the United States market for something that has no existence outside a server.
suggested_refs: The IGE Shanghai office and the Chinese gold-farming supply chain of the mid-2000s

stops.name: Central, Hong Kong, sixty million and a man from Goldman
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 2006; day set to 01 by convention
stops.campa: In February 2006 the company closes a sixty million dollar investment round, found with the help of a banker named Steve Bannon whom Pierce has brought in for exactly that purpose. Twenty million of it goes to Pierce personally, for a minority stake. He is twenty-five years old and has now been paid twice over: once for a childhood spent in front of cameras, once for a business in currencies that do not exist. Bannon is placed on the board as a condition of the Goldman Sachs investment.
suggested_refs: The February 2006 Goldman Sachs-brokered investment round in IGE

stops.name: Central, Hong Kong, the class action and the succession
stops.date_confidence: class action filed May 2007, Bannon's replacement of Pierce as chief executive attested to June 2007; days set to 01 by convention. Several accounts compress these events into the February 2006 funding, sixteen months earlier, and that compression is not followed here
stops.campa: In May 2007 a player named Antonio Hernandez files a class action against the company on behalf of World of Warcraft subscribers, arguing that the gold trade spoils the game they pay a subscription to play. In June, Steve Bannon replaces Pierce as chief executive, having taken his seat on the board on the strength of the money he brought in the year before. The founder is out of his own company sixteen months after that round, removed by the man he hired to save it. He is twenty-six. He keeps the twenty million dollars.
suggested_refs: Hernandez v. Internet Gaming Entertainment, filed May 2007

stops.name: Los Angeles, the board of Titan Gaming
stops.date_confidence: the board recruitment is attested to 2010 without a month; the stop carries the 2011 Xfire separation and the April 2012 Playsino rebrand with it. No source names a city for these companies, and the Los Angeles pin follows his attested base rather than a stated address
stops.campa: Three years pass in which the record has very little to say about him. In 2010 he is recruited onto the board of Titan Gaming. Its subsidiary Xfire takes four million dollars from Intel Capital in October 2011 and is separated out; in April 2012 what remains rebrands as Playsino, with Pierce as chief executive and one and a half million dollars behind it. These are smaller rooms than the one in Hong Kong. He is thirty-one. The money from Hong Kong is five years old and he is still in games.
suggested_refs: Titan Gaming, Xfire and Playsino, 2010-2012

stops.name: Shenzhen, Tencent takes the network
stops.date_confidence: the acquisition is attested to March 2012; the Shenzhen pin is inferred from Tencent's headquarters and is not stated as the locus of the deal in any reachable source. Day set to 01 by convention
stops.campa: ZAM, the network of gaming websites Pierce founded in 2003, is acquired in March 2012 by Tencent. The price is not published. ZAM was the respectable half of the operation: databases, guides, forums, the encyclopedic apparatus that grew up around games in the years when players still wrote their own documentation, unpaid, for each other. It goes to the largest game company on earth. Pierce is thirty-one and, for the first time since he was twenty, out of the industry that made him.
suggested_refs: The ZAM Network, founded 2003, sold to Tencent March 2012

stops.name: San Francisco, Blockchain Capital
stops.date_confidence: founding attested to 2013, month set to 01 by convention; San Francisco is the fund's publicly known base and was not independently reverified. The Mastercoin work is attested to the same year with no location given at all
stops.campa: He co-founds Blockchain Capital with Bart and Bradford Stephens, first named Crypto Currency Partners, one of the earliest venture funds built to hold nothing but digital assets. Through it he assists Jeffrey Epstein in placing money into cryptocurrency companies, Coinbase among them. The same year he works on the Mastercoin offering, the first sale of a token to fund the protocol the token runs on, and every initial coin offering that follows copies its shape. He is thirty-two.
suggested_refs: The Mastercoin token sale of 2013, template for the ICO

stops.name: Tokyo, an offer for the wreck
stops.date_confidence: the Sunlot Holdings offer is attested to March 2014; the Tokyo pin is the venue of the Mt. Gox bankruptcy proceedings and not an attested presence for Pierce. Day set to 01 by convention
stops.campa: Mt. Gox, which had handled most of the world's bitcoin trading, collapses in February 2014 with hundreds of thousands of customer coins gone. In March, Pierce's Sunlot Holdings files an offer to buy what remains: the estate, the claims, the ruined name. The bid does not carry. Why it fails, and what Sunlot was offering, the reachable record does not say. The bankruptcy proceedings run on in Tokyo for another decade, and the creditors who filed in 2014 are still waiting on distributions.
suggested_refs: The Mt. Gox bankruptcy estate and the 2014 Sunlot Holdings bid

stops.name: Washington, appointed to the Bitcoin Foundation
stops.date_confidence: attested to May 2014; day set to 01 by convention. Sources differ on whether he was elected a director or appointed to the board alongside Bobby Lee, and the count of resignations is given as ten, with a further nine after the May elections, rather than the vaguer 'several' that appears elsewhere
stops.campa: In May 2014 Pierce takes a seat on the board of the Bitcoin Foundation, the Washington body that then spoke for the protocol and paid several of its core developers. Ten members resign over the allegations that have followed him since Santa Monica; nine more go after the elections. The Foundation exists to steward a network whose first transaction, ten coins sent as a test, was received by Hal Finney on the second machine ever to run the software. Pierce keeps the seat.
suggested_refs: The Bitcoin Foundation board resignations of 2014

stops.name: Santa Monica, Realcoin
stops.date_confidence: the Realcoin announcement is attested to July 2014; day set to 01 by convention. The quoted phrase is attributed to Pierce by a July 2020 report that could not be fetched directly and is carried here as reported speech
stops.campa: Realcoin is announced in Santa Monica in July 2014 by Pierce, Reeve Collins and Craig Sellars: a token that would always be worth one dollar, backed one for one by dollars held in reserve. It is renamed Tether. Whatever is argued afterwards about the reserves, and a great deal is argued, the object does the thing it was built to do, which is let a person hold a dollar inside a system that contains no banks. Pierce says his own involvement ended in 2015.
stops.quote: one of the most important innovations in currency
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Pierce describing Tether, reported July 2020
suggested_refs: The Realcoin announcement of July 2014 and its renaming as Tether

stops.name: Road Town, Tortola, where the issuer is registered
stops.date_confidence: the British Virgin Islands incorporation of Tether Holdings Limited is attested to 2014 without a month; the month here orders the segment
stops.campa: Tether Holdings Limited is incorporated in the British Virgin Islands, at Road Town on Tortola. The company issuing the dollar token is not in Santa Monica and not in the United States. It is a registered address on an island of registered addresses, in a jurisdiction with no capital gains tax and a light disclosure regime. This is not a scandal in 2014; it is ordinary practice. The token will circulate on exchanges everywhere. The company that issues it is a name on a registry in Road Town.
suggested_refs: Tether Holdings Limited, registered in the British Virgin Islands

stops.name: Washington, the Foundation nearly insolvent
stops.date_confidence: the disclosure is attested to 2015 without a month, and the month here orders the segment. Some accounts say the Foundation announced insolvency in July 2015; the reachable record says instead that a board member publicly revealed it was nearly insolvent, which prompted layoffs, and that weaker statement is the one carried here
stops.campa: A board member, Olivier Janssens, publishes that the Bitcoin Foundation is nearly insolvent. Staff are laid off. The organization that had been the closest thing bitcoin possessed to an institution never recovers its authority, and the protocol carries on without an institution, which is what a good number of the people who built it wanted from the beginning. No successor body is chartered. Pierce had held a seat on that board for eleven months, at the cost of nineteen other people's resignations.
suggested_refs: Olivier Janssens's 2015 disclosure of the Bitcoin Foundation's finances

segments.name: Cayman, San Juan, and the Four Billion Dollar Offering

stops.name: George Town, Grand Cayman, Block.one registered
stops.date_confidence: the Cayman registration and the June 2017 start of the token sale are attested; day set to 01 by convention. Coordinates are those of George Town itself, the island's registered-office district, not of any named building
stops.campa: Block.one is registered in the Cayman Islands and begins, in June 2017, the longest token sale ever run: a year of continuous distribution that raises more than four billion dollars for software called EOS.IO, a platform for programs that execute themselves on a public ledger. Nick Szabo had given such programs their name, smart contracts, more than twenty years earlier, writing in Amsterdam for David Chaum's digital cash company. Pierce is chief strategy officer of the company that collects the money.
suggested_refs: The EOS.IO token distribution, June 2017 to June 2018

stops.name: Old San Juan, after the hurricane
stops.date_confidence: the relocation to Puerto Rico is attested to 2017 without a month; the month here places it after Hurricane Maria's September landfall, which the sources treat as the context for the crypto migration
stops.campa: Pierce moves to Puerto Rico in 2017. The island's tax status for qualifying new residents is the reason most of the arrivals give and the reason he will later give himself, in writing, to explain a decision he does not make. Hurricane Maria comes ashore in September and takes the electrical grid down for months. The crypto arrivals who follow him describe what they are doing as a recovery. The reporters coin a word for it, Puertopia. The people who were already living there use other words.
suggested_refs: Nellie Bowles, 'Making a Crypto Utopia in Puerto Rico,' New York Times, February 2018

stops.name: Old San Juan, the monastery
stops.date_confidence: attested to 2018, month set to 01 by convention. The building is described in the sources only as a former monastery in Old San Juan; an identification with the Hotel El Convento circulates but is unsupported by the cited reporting and by the hotel's own record, and is not made here. The pin is Old San Juan generally
stops.campa: By 2018 he has taken a former monastery building in the old city and made it a headquarters: offices, a place to receive people, a courtyard, four centuries of stone. Which building it is the reporting does not say, and one identification that circulates does not survive checking. Nellie Bowles comes down for the New York Times in February and writes about a utopia being planned by men who arrived with money on an island that had just lost its power. That same month Forbes puts Pierce among the twenty wealthiest people in cryptocurrency, somewhere between seven hundred million and one point one billion dollars.
suggested_refs: The unnamed former monastery in Old San Juan converted to a headquarters, 2018

stops.name: George Town, the resignation
stops.date_confidence: attested to March 2018; day set to 01 by convention
stops.campa: In March 2018 Pierce resigns as chief strategy officer of Block.one with the token sale still running. Three months of the year-long distribution remain. No reason survives in the record, from him or from the company. The offering finishes above four billion dollars, the largest in the history of the form, and the company that holds the money continues without the man who had been its face. He is thirty-seven years old, and what he takes with him out of it the record does not say.
suggested_refs: Block.one after the EOS distribution

stops.name: New York, 2307 Broadway
stops.date_confidence: announcement attested to 5 July 2020 and the FEC filing to 7 July; the Broadway address is taken from a campaign photograph whose caption names only New York City, and the coordinates are those of the street address itself
stops.campa: On the fifth of July, 2020, Pierce announces an independent campaign for President of the United States, and files with the Federal Election Commission two days later. The headquarters is a storefront at 2307 Broadway on the Upper West Side. Karla Ballard is his running mate. He is thirty-nine, four years past the constitutional minimum, and he tells interviewers plainly that the campaign's own arithmetic does not require him to win a national election.
stops.quote: You don't have to win to become president.
stops.quote_source: Brock Pierce, interview with Cointelegraph, 20 August 2020
suggested_refs: The campaign headquarters at 2307 Broadway, Manhattan

stops.name: Oklahoma City, the first ballot
stops.date_confidence: the Oklahoma ballot access date is attested; Oklahoma City stands for the state's administrative seat, and no source places Pierce or his staff physically at any filing
stops.campa: Ten days after filing, the campaign secures ballot access in Oklahoma, the first of the states. Independent access is a paperwork discipline before it is anything else: signatures gathered to a state threshold, filed by a state deadline, in a summer when nobody wants a clipboard held out to them. Arkansas follows on the twelfth of August, Colorado on the nineteenth. Nobody from the campaign is attested at any of these filings in person. A ballot line is a document arriving at a secretary of state's office.
suggested_refs: The 2020 independent ballot-access thresholds, state by state

stops.name: New York, the Independence Party line
stops.date_confidence: the nomination is attested to 24 August 2020
stops.campa: On the twenty-fourth of August the Independence Party of New York nominates him, the only established party line the campaign obtains. Tim Draper endorses him. So does Akon. The plan, which he states openly in interviews and does not hedge, is not a plan for winning a national election: win three states, deny both major candidates a majority in the Electoral College, and send the choice to the House of Representatives, where the states vote one delegation apiece.
stops.quote: If a third party such as myself were to win a single state, it becomes possible that no one wins the election. If a third party such as again, ourselves, were to win three states, it becomes likely that no one wins the election. So I'm not trying to win the election. I'm trying to win three states so that no one wins the election.
stops.quote_source: Brock Pierce, interview with Cointelegraph, 20 August 2020
suggested_refs: The Independence Party of New York nomination, August 2020

stops.name: Denver, the second open debate
stops.date_confidence: attested to 8 October 2020. Colorado ballot access is separately attested to 19 August, but that was a filing and no source places him in the state that month
stops.campa: Colorado had put him on its ballot on the nineteenth of August, by document. On the eighth of October he is in Denver in person, at the Second Open Presidential Debate, the stage that exists because the Commission on Presidential Debates does not invite candidates polling under fifteen percent. The other names on the platform are the other names nobody has heard of. It is the only nationally staged debate his campaign appears in, and it is staged by Free and Equal rather than by the Commission.
stops.quote: I'm running with a strategy to end up in the White House in January.
stops.quote_source: Brock Pierce, interview with Cointelegraph, 20 August 2020
suggested_refs: The Free and Equal Second Open Presidential Debate, Denver, 8 October 2020

stops.name: Provo, one vote on a chain
stops.date_confidence: attested to 13 October 2020; the coordinates are Provo, the seat of Utah County
stops.campa: On the thirteenth of October a ballot is cast for Pierce in Utah County through Voatz, a smartphone application that records votes on a blockchain, and the campaign announces that he is the first presidential candidate in history to receive one. Utah County had been running the application as a pilot for overseas voters and voters with disabilities, which is the only reason the machinery was standing there to be used. The claim is precise and the claim is true. The total is one vote.
suggested_refs: The Voatz pilot in Utah County, 2020

stops.name: Cheyenne, the Independent National Convention
stops.date_confidence: the convention is attested to 23-24 October 2020 at Cheyenne; the announcement from Casper is attested to 2020 without a month and is carried inside this stop rather than given its own
stops.campa: He had announced it from Casper. It convenes in Cheyenne on the twenty-third and twenty-fourth of October: an Independent National Convention, called by a candidate belonging to no party, in the least populous state in the union. Wyoming is the one state where his is the only independent name on the ballot. Under the campaign's own theory of the Electoral College that makes it the most winnable state on the map, and the theory needs three of them. Wyoming casts three electoral votes.
suggested_refs: The Independent National Convention, Cheyenne, 23-24 October 2020

stops.name: Old San Juan, three hundredths of one percent
stops.date_confidence: the vote share is attested to the general election of 3 November 2020; no source places Pierce anywhere on election night, and the pin is his attested residence rather than an attested location
stops.campa: On the third of November he receives roughly three hundredths of one percent of the national vote. No state is won, not Wyoming and not any of the others. No delegation of the House of Representatives is called upon to choose anything at all. Twelve days earlier he had told an interviewer that everyone in the space believes in decentralization and that nobody is there yet, that what exists in the meantime is a step upward, and the reporter wrote down the word he had used for it, which was staircase.
stops.quote: All of us in this space generally believe in decentralization. The reality is that it is just more practical in the short term. We're not there yet.
suggested_refs: The 2020 United States presidential election returns for independent candidates

stops.name: Washington, the schoolhouse on Maryland Avenue
stops.date_confidence: the purchase is attested to 2020 without a month, and the month here orders the segment; the coordinates are those of the Pierce School Lofts at 1375 Maryland Avenue Northeast. A claim that the building is named for President Franklin Pierce appears in no source consulted and is not carried here
stops.campa: Sometime in 2020 he buys a penthouse loft on Maryland Avenue Northeast in Washington from the basketball player Dwight Howard, for about two million dollars. The building went up in 1893 as a public school and is now called the Pierce School Lofts, which is a coincidence of surname and nothing else, whatever gets said about it. He has run for the presidency and lost it by three orders of magnitude, and he buys a schoolhouse in the city he ran to govern. The month of the sale is not published anywhere reachable.
suggested_refs: The Pierce School Lofts, 1375 Maryland Avenue Northeast, built 1893

stops.name: San Salvador, the delegation
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 2021; day set to 01 by convention
stops.campa: In June 2021 Pierce leads an international delegation to El Salvador, advising a government that is about to make bitcoin legal tender alongside the dollar, the first country anywhere to do it. He holds no office in El Salvador and none in the United States. The delegation is not a diplomatic instrument and does not pretend to be one. It is a group of people with money and firm opinions about money, invited in by a president who wants both. The same month he co-founds Roundtable Media with James Heckman and David Bailey.
suggested_refs: El Salvador's Bitcoin Law of June 2021

stops.name: Brooklyn, the gaming trucks
stops.date_confidence: the unveiling is attested to 20 October 2021 by a local television report; some summaries date the initiative to December 2021, and that later date is not followed here
stops.campa: In October 2021 he funds a New York Police Department initiative and stands with officers in Brooklyn as they unveil gaming trucks to schoolchildren. The vans are fitted out with consoles and screens and driven into a neighborhood to be opened on the street. A local news crew films it. He made his first fortune in the currencies of video games and sold out of that trade at twenty-six. Now he is handing controllers to children while the department stands beside him.
suggested_refs: ABC7 Eyewitness News, 20 October 2021, on the NYPD gaming trucks

stops.name: Montpelier, the Senate that was not run for
stops.date_confidence: the FEC statement is attested to November 2021; day set to 01 by convention. Montpelier, the state capital, stands in for a filing whose physical location the sources do not name, and no source places Pierce in Vermont
stops.campa: In November 2021 he files a statement with the Federal Election Commission for a United States Senate seat in Vermont, the seat Patrick Leahy is vacating. He never files to qualify for the ballot. The reason given is that running would put his Puerto Rico tax residency at risk. He weighs a Senate seat against a tax residency in public and says which one he keeps. No source places him in Vermont at any point, and whether the seat was ever more than a filing the record does not say.
suggested_refs: The 2022 Vermont Senate race and Patrick Leahy's retirement

stops.name: Anatevka, the foundation stone
stops.date_confidence: attested to March 2025; day set to 01 by convention. The coordinates follow the mapped location of Anatevka near Hnativka and Bilohorodka, west of Kyiv
stops.campa: In March 2025, in the village of Anatevka west of Kyiv, Pierce and the Chief Rabbi of Ukraine, Moshe Azman, lay together the foundation stone of a business school. Azman founded the village in 2015 as a refuge for Jews displaced inside Ukraine and named it for the shtetl in Sholem Aleichem, the village whose whole literary existence is that it gets left. Three years into a full-scale war, two men set a stone in the ground for a school meant to teach people how to start companies.

stops.campa: On the twenty-third of September, 2025, at the MGM National Harbor resort on the Maryland bank of the Potomac, Pierce presents an award to the pastor Mark Burns at a gala segment of something calling itself the Ukraine Reconstruction Summit. The event's own website describes a forum for officials and investors on rebuilding the country. No independent news organization is on record covering any part of it. What survives is a single video, shot in the ballroom, in which he reads out a name and hands the award across a lectern.
